quote.text:
S&P Dow Jones Indices and Kalshi are joining forces to build the next generation of financial markets.

The Dow launched in 1896. The S&P 500 in 1957. The idea was simple: bring individual stocks together into a single benchmark, giving people a clearer view of the broader market.

Over time, products built around those benchmarks transformed investing. Index funds, ETFs, futures, and options gave investors ways to gain diversified market exposure and hedge broad market swings.

These indices became foundations of global finance. More than $20 trillion is indexed or benchmarked to the S&P 500 alone.

Today, this structure extends beyond stocks to bonds, commodities, currencies, and more.

The next step is to bring that structure to the events that shape everyone’s lives.

Through this partnership, S&P Dow Jones Indices and Kalshi will work together to create indices composed of Kalshi event contracts.

Think about what that opens up.

An index of political power. An index of supply chain risk. An index tracking AI’s impact on employment. An index of sports outcomes that affect broadcasters, advertisers, cities, and small businesses. An index of weather risks that shape harvests, energy demand, and business revenues.

Each would bundle event contracts into a single indicator, helping people understand how related risks are evolving.

Over time, products built around these indices could offer diversified exposure to those events and new ways to hedge their impact.

The events that shape our lives could become as easy to track and gain exposure to as the S&P 500.

the level everyone was terrified of becomes support.

and the same people shorting $80k will be explaining why $100k was inevitable.

i'm not calling the bottom. but I started buying again.

$BTC Big week(s).

Either Bitcoin holds $80K throughout these next 1-2 weeks with: FOMC, Earnings, Election(s), IPO filing(s), End/Start of the month flows & whatever geopolitical headlines we're going to see.

In that case I think we go to $87K and take out those equal highs there and target $90K+.

If price does lose $80K we'll find ourselves in a solid high timeframe value area (I think) in the mid to low $70Ks. Might chop around there for a while and things will look scary. But from there I do believe we have a good chance of setting that higher timeframe higher low from the big impulse from $58K to the recent high at $87K.

Best to keep an eye on the headlines and see how the market reacts. That will be leading.

I think sentiment and outlook is pretty bearish already so if we were to absorb whatever selling happens down here and prices just start grinding up that'd be a big sign of strength to me and at that case I think this will just keep drifting up by shorts covering and sidelined/derisked capital moving back in over the days.

It's going to be very easy to get chopped up or shaken out of your bias in the next 1-2 weeks I think.

Easiest to just play things level by level and go from there. Don't assume supports or resistances break until you actually see it broken (on a daily candle close for example). That is how many people keep getting caught off guard.

#Bitcoin – What’s Next?

The Big Sunday Report: All We Need to Know

TA / LCA / Psychological Breakdown

I have finished building the long positions I announced and entered between $80K and $81K. My average entry is now $80,400 for the longs, while my average spot entry is between 60-64k. Remember the sequence: My earlier predictions called a breakout above $82,500, followed by $88K, and it happened, and the time I made the prediction Bitcoin was trading at 60k. After the move into that target area, I prepared for the correction. At $88K, when everyone was calling for $100K, I was calling for $79K. Bitcoin did indeed crash to $80K, so I closed my entire short at $80,600, bought more Bitcoin spot and opened a long at that same price. I stopped waiting for the exact $79K target. The short served its purpose. It was a correction WITHIN a bull market, not my announcement of another bear market. To this day, BTC is still trading in the region I identified when it was at $88K. This tells me one thing: the $80K–$81K area, even extending down to $79K, is an accumulation zone. This can be observed clearly: spot demand is higher in this region, while long positions are also being built. If we analyse retail behaviour at this stage, we notice that MOST retail traders are extremely bearish. I will discuss this further below.

The $80K area is also a VERY IMPORTANT support level for bigger players, and this is something smaller retail players ignore. The average buying cost of Bitcoin for treasuries is at $80,200, with treasury and US spot ETF average entry buys are around $80K–$81.5K. It also reported that Binance spot bids around $80K had rebuilt by October 20 after the earlier correction from $88k. Meanwhile, realized profit-taking had slowed to roughly half its pace around the September high. Overall, this means the average entry of institutional investors sits around $80K–$81.5K, and profit-taking has slowed significantly. This tells me that the current selling pressure is coming from retail investors, combined with short positions in the futures market, while spot selling can be seen at the current prices from short term holders, but mid and long term holders do not dare to sell their BTC they bought at 60-70k. These conditions usually occur at local bottoms, and this is exactly why I am going long in the $80K–$81K region.

Now compare this with market sentiment. The Fear & Greed Index is at 54, but I question this reading because I see much more fear in the market right now. The reason is very simple: the Fear & Greed Index uses a calculation model, and most investors who purchased BTC in the last two to three months are currently sitting in profit. Those investors are experienced because they bought the bottom, they knew when to enter, its correct to call it smart money, while inexperienced investors have either not entered the market yet or are among those who sold in the last few days. To make my point clear: if BTC were at $120K right now, retail concentration in BTC would be high, the Fear & Greed Index’s formula would place BTC in the fear zone. However, there has not been much panic selling from experienced investors so far, only a large number of weak hands have been shaken out. So the Fear and Greed formula analyses 100% of the BTC owners behaviour, and sees that the 80% of experienced traders are holding and not scared. But if the Fear and Greed would be applied on the remaining 20% in the market, which are a massive minority, the fear and greed would be at extreme fear levels right now.

Now I explained you my points why I believe this is the bottom region, and I hope it makes sense. I keep holding my spot positions from 60-64k, and my longs from 80-81k and my target is the area of 94k. What I would love to see now is BTC reclaiming the EMA50 and close the daily above, and even if it does not, it becomes an indicator the bears can use and nothing else. I am confident that this is the local bottom

This week’s calendar is HOT: we have the FOMC decision on October 28. The numbers show an 89.7% probability of unchanged rates and a 10.3% probability of a quarter-point hike. My live entries, additions and position updates are shared exclusively in Premium.(http://DrProfitCrypto.com)

THIS IS NOT FINANCIAL ADVICE, BUT EDUCATIONAL CONTENT ONLY.

$BTC Has meanwhile moved back to its 2 year moving average price after deviating below it for some time.

In my previous tweet I mentioned how Bitcoin tends to. historically trade at good high timeframe value when it is below that level. The big question is usually how long it remains below that area. In this case it didn't take a long time because since then, price moved up from $63K to $87K at its recent high in just 3 months.

Good reason why I always like to keep looking at these high timeframe "indicators" to determine when BTC is at historically good value levels.

quote.text:
$BTC 2-Year MA Multiplier is signaling that Bitcoin is in its value area.

All this does is see if Bitcoin trades below its 2 year moving average. Everything underneath, marked in green, is usually considered good long term value. It marked the bottom in every cycle so far, but as you can see with a big note. Last cycle it traded down there for almost 1.5 years and extended up to -30% deeper.

So take it with a big grain of salt.

But we can all agree that these valuations make more sense than if price were to be trading near its 2 year moving average x5 (red line) which has roughly marked the top in every cycle except the last one.
